MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 23, 2025

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR STEGURA called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Evelyn Calip, Breast Oncology Nurse & Founder of Non-Profit Evelyn’s Breast Friends
Forever (BFF).

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Development/Public Works Director Naughton
  Assistant to the City Manager Jessica Slawson
  Administrative Aide Gabrielle Swain

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING  OCTOBER  2025  "BREAST  CANCER
  AWARENESS MONTH"

MAYOR STEGURA declared October 2025 as “Breast Cancer Awareness Month,” and
presented the proclamation to Evelyn Calip, Breast Oncology Nurse & Founder of Non-Profit
Evelyn’s BFFs.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-E AS FOLLOWS BY
  THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  APPROVED.

B.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT OF AUGUST 2025

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

C.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF AUGUST 2025

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 9, 2025

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
SEPTEMBER 23, 2025
 E.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 8, 2025

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT/PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

None.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

None.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 2608 UPDATING THE POLICY REGARDING THE
  PROCUREMENT OF EQUIPMENT, GOODS, AND SERVICES

  Recommendation: That City Council adopt Resolution No. 2608 updating the policy
  for the procurement of equipment, goods, and services.

Assistant City Manager Davis and City Attorney Davis provided a staff report (as per the
agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2608 UPDATING THE POLICY FOR THE
  PROCUREMENT OF EQUIPMENT, GOODS, AND SERVICES.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

Administrative Aide Swain read Resolution 2608 by title.

B.  ADOPTION OF FY 2025-26 PUBLICLY AVAILABLE PAY SCHEDULE

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Fiscal Year 2025-26 California
  Public Employees' Retirement System (CalPERS) “Publicly Available Pay Schedule.”

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  APPROVE THE FISCAL YEAR 2025-26 CALIFORNIA PUBLIC EMPLOYEES'
  RETIREMENT SYSTEM (CALPERS) “PUBLICLY AVAILABLE PAY
  SCHEDULE.”

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
SEPTEMBER 23, 2025
 9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 754 REPEALING
  CHAPTER 8.08 OF THE ROLLING HILLS MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO
  ALARM SYSTEMS

  Recommendation: That the City Council conduct the second reading and adopt
  Ordinance No. 754.

Community Development & Public Works Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per
the agenda material).

MAYOR STEGURA noted her concerns about this Ordinance leading to false alarms
burdening the Sheriff’s Department.

Community Development & Public Works Director Naughton explained that there would be
no change in the level of service provided by the Sheriff’s Department and would be no
additional costs; that this change would remove the administrative burden on staff to
administer the program without being able to recoup the costs, in response to MAYOR PRO
TEM ZERUNYAN. City Manager Grammer further explained that residents would no longer
need to apply for home alarm system permits, and the City would no longer have a
mechanism to fine for false alarm permits.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  CONDUCT SECOND READING AND ADOPT ORDINANCE NO. 754.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan
  NOES:  Stegura
  ABSENT:  None

Administrative Aide Swain read Ordinance No. 754 by title.

B.  QUARTERLY WORK PLAN UPDATE

  Recommendation: Receive and file.

City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), including an
update on the George F Canyon Nature Center project, Palos Verdes Drive North &
Dapplegray School Improvement project, the Multijurisdictional Hazard Mitigation Plan,
upgrades to the Council Chamber, Street Resurfacing project, updated Procurement Policy,
Film Ordinance, and Ernie Howlett Tennis Club pilot program.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

MAYOR STEGURA so ordered.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
SEPTEMBER 23, 2025
 11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ thanked Congregation Ner Tamid for the invitation to Rosh
Hashanah services today, which she and MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN attended, and
wished all those who celebrate a Happy New Year.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

MAYOR STEGURA announced that the City won the annual volleyball match against the
Lomita Sheriff’s Station at the Annual City Celebration on September 13.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN explained that he has recently been diagnosed with throat
and tongue cancer and would be undergoing treatment in the coming months.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED LITIGATION Government
  Code Section 54956.9(d)(2)
  Significant exposure to litigation: one potential case

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 7:26 p.m. MAYOR STEGURA adjourned the meeting in memory of Palos Verdes
Peninsula Library District Trustee, Robert Parke and Evelyn Whitehead. The meeting was
adjourned to Tuesday, October 14, 2025 at 7:00 p.m. for the purpose of a regular meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit, City Clerk  Debby Stegura, Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
SEPTEMBER 23, 2025
